To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of ultrasound guidance in the ED for internal jugular central venous cannulation is associated with higher success rates, fewer complications and a shorter learning curve compared to the use of the traditional landmark technique.

real-time ultrasonography-guidance of internal jugular central venous access is associated with a significantly higher first attempt success (82.0% vs. 70.6%; P ¼ 0.04) and higher overall success rate (93% vs. 78.5%; P ¼.01) compared with landmark guidance in an emergency department setting.

the ultrasonographic guidance technique for internal jugular line placement is superior to the landmark technique for success rate, first-attempt success rate, time to venipuncture, time to catheter placement, and complication rate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a new method of ultrasonography-guidance for internal jugular venipuncture.
the development of an ultrasonographic approach to internal jugular vein central venous catheters.
the development of a new approach to the development of the ultrasonographic guidance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

ultrasonographic guidance of internal jugular venous catheter insertion is superior to the landmark method and that it should be considered a desirable practice alternative for EDs that have ultrasonographic capability.

real-time ultrasonography-guidance of internal jugular catheterization is an educational imperative, an alternative to the traditional landmark technique, a desirable practice standard, and a practice standard in the making.
ultrasonography is a useful adjunct to internal jugular vein access.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the development and implementation of ultrasonographic training programs for ED personnel will improve patient safety and enhance the quality of care.
we are in the process of learning how to do it right, and that the use of ultrasonography in the ED will help to ensure that we do it right.
we have demonstrated that ultrasonography is safe and efficacious in the ED and should be the preferred technique for the placement of central venous catheters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ultrasound-guided central line placement is safe and effective, but it requires practice, training and a commitment to excellence.
the use of real-time ultrasonography for internal jugular venous cannulation is an effective and safe technique for ED use, and that it should become the standard for this procedure.
ultrasound-guided internal jugular vein access in the ED is safe, effective, and feasible.
